text:
The sympathetic supply to the colon originates from preganglionic neurons in the intermediolateral cell column of the thoracolumbar cord, roughly T10–L2, which travel through the thoracic and lumbar splanchnic nerves to synapse in the celiac, superior mesenteric, and inferior mesenteric ganglia. The shared team note is wrong: sympathetic output does not come from the lumbosacral cord, because the sacral segments (S2–S4) are parasympathetic (pelvic splanchnic nerves) and sympathetic outflow ends around L2. That error should be corrected before it spreads.

CONFIDENCE: 80
